machine_profile.summary: Generic template for textile dyeing and finishing machinery: jet and soft-flow dyeing machines, stenters, thermal-oil heaters and steam boilers that supply process heat.
machine_profile.typical_duty: Batch dyeing cycles of 4 to 10 hours at 60 to 135 C, continuous stenter drying and heat-setting at 150 to 210 C, boilers and heaters running 20 to 24 hours a day.

operating_parameters.label: Stack oxygen
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: Higher O2 means excess air and wasted fuel; lower means incomplete combustion and soot.

operating_parameters.label: Stack gas temperature
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: A rise of 20 C at the same load signals fouled heat-transfer surfaces.

operating_parameters.label: Steam header pressure
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: Unstable pressure lengthens dye cycles and wastes fuel.

operating_parameters.label: Liquor ratio
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: Higher ratios raise water, chemical and energy use per kg.

operating_parameters.label: Dye-bath temperature
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: Overshoot damages fabric and wastes energy; undershoot causes shade variation and re-dyeing.

operating_parameters.label: Thermal-oil outlet temperature
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: Overheating cracks the oil and fouls coils.

operating_parameters.label: Stenter fabric speed
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: Speed loss at the same temperature means drying capacity is lost.

operating_parameters.label: Effluent pH at machine drain
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: Out-of-range pH stresses the effluent treatment plant and may breach discharge limits.

operating_parameters.label: Fuel firing rate
operating_parameters.why_it_matters: Fuel per tonne of steam or per metre of fabric is the core efficiency metric.

job_types.name: Burner and combustion tune-up
job_types.trigger: Every 2,000 operating hours, or when stack O2 drifts more than 1.5 points
checklist: Isolate fuel and power
Remove and clean the nozzle, swirler and diffuser
Check the ignition electrode gap
Inspect the flame scanner lens
Re-set the air-fuel ratio with a flue-gas analyser at low, mid and high fire
Record O2, CO and stack temperature after tuning
safety_and_permit_notes: Lock-out / tag-out and zero-energy verification before opening
Fuel-line isolation and leak test on reassembly
Heat-resistant gloves and face shield; allow cooling to below 50 C

job_types.name: Heat-exchanger and coil descaling
job_types.trigger: Approach temperature up 5 C, or annually
checklist: Isolate and drain the exchanger
Open the end covers and inspect the tubes
Circulate an inhibited descaling solution or clean mechanically
Neutralise and flush
Pressure-test before return to service
safety_and_permit_notes: Lock-out / tag-out and zero-energy verification before opening
Chemical handling PPE and an eyewash station
Neutralised spent solution goes to the ETP, never the storm drain

job_types.name: Circulation pump mechanical-seal replacement
job_types.trigger: Visible leak, or seal age over 8,000 hours
checklist: Isolate and drain the pump casing
Remove the coupling and the bearing housing
Replace the mechanical seal and O-rings
Check shaft run-out (below 0.05 mm)
Re-align the coupling with a laser tool
safety_and_permit_notes: Lock-out / tag-out and zero-energy verification before opening
Hot dye liquor: drain and cool first
Spill tray under the pump

job_types.name: Stenter chain, clip, padder and rail overhaul
job_types.trigger: Chain elongation above 2%, padder nip variation above 10%, or every 6 months
checklist: Measure chain elongation over ten links
Replace worn clips and pins
Clean and lubricate rails with high-temperature grease
Check padder roll parallelism and nip pressure
Run a fabric-width test
safety_and_permit_notes: Lock-out / tag-out and zero-energy verification before opening
Guarding back in place before the trial run
Burn risk from hot chamber panels

job_types.name: Boiler / heater refractory patch repair
job_types.trigger: Casing hot spot above 80 C, or visible cracks at inspection
checklist: Cool the furnace below 50 C
Remove loose refractory
Apply anchors where needed
Cast or gun castable refractory
Dry out on a controlled heat-up curve
safety_and_permit_notes: Confined-space entry permit, gas test and standby attendant
Hot-work permit if cutting, welding or grinding
Dust mask for refractory dust

job_types.name: Air filter, strainer and lint-screen cleaning
job_types.trigger: Filter differential pressure above the set limit, or weekly
checklist: Isolate the fan
Remove and clean or replace the intake filter
Clean the lint screens and the fuel strainer
Check the filter housing seals
Record the differential pressure after cleaning
safety_and_permit_notes: Lock-out / tag-out and zero-energy verification before opening
Lint is combustible: keep away from hot surfaces

job_types.name: Effluent drain, dosing and colour-carryover check
job_types.trigger: Effluent colour or pH out of range, or monthly
checklist: Inspect the drain valve and seals for leaks
Check the dye-bath drop sequence and the rinse count
Verify the dosing-pump stroke
Take a grab sample for colour and pH
Record the volume per batch
safety_and_permit_notes: Chemical-resistant gloves and goggles
Slippery floor: use a wet-area mat

job_types.name: Instrument and dosing-pump calibration
job_types.trigger: Reading drift beyond tolerance, or every 6 months
checklist: Calibrate temperature and pressure transmitters against a reference
Calibrate the dosing pumps by a timed volume test
Check the controller loop tuning
Update the calibration labels and records
safety_and_permit_notes: Inform operators before forcing signals
Permit to work on live control panels

job_types.name: Steam-trap and condensate-return survey
checklist: Test every trap with an ultrasonic or temperature method
Tag failed-open and failed-closed traps
Replace failed traps
Check the condensate pump and tank vent
safety_and_permit_notes: Live steam: isolate and depressurise
Heat-resistant gloves and face shield; allow cooling to below 50 C

job_types.name: Thermal-oil sampling, analysis and top-up or change
job_types.trigger: Annually, or when the oil darkens or smells cracked
checklist: Take a hot sample from the circulating line
Send it for viscosity, acid number and flash point tests
Vent low-boilers through the expansion tank
Top up or change the oil per the lab result
safety_and_permit_notes: Hot oil burns: sample with a cooler
Fire watch while handling oil near the heater

job_types.name: Exhaust and combustion-air fan service
checklist: Measure vibration on both bearings
Clean the impeller of lint and deposits
Check the belt tension or the coupling
Balance the impeller if vibration persists
Re-grease the bearings
safety_and_permit_notes: Lock-out / tag-out and zero-energy verification before opening
Wait for the impeller to stop completely

snag_types.name: Burner fouling
symptoms: Yellow or smoky flame
Soot on the nozzle and the furnace tubes
Stack O2 or CO outside the tuned band with higher fuel use
root_causes: Poor fuel atomisation from a worn nozzle
snag_types.detection_method: Visual flame check plus flue-gas analysis of O2 and CO against the last tuning record

severity_levels.definition: First sign of burner fouling: yellow or smoky flame noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: yellow or smoky flame confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: soot on the nozzle and the furnace tubes; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: stack o2 or co outside the tuned band with higher fuel use; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.

Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate to the combustion engineer if CO stays above 200 ppm after cleaning or the flame is unstable

snag_types.immediate_action: Reduce the firing rate, check the fuel temperature and filter, and book the burner service
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate to the combustion engineer if CO stays above 200 ppm after cleaning or the flame is unstable

pollution_effects.effect: Incomplete combustion raises CO2 per unit of steam, NOx variability and particulate emissions.

snag_types.name: Refractory wear
symptoms: Hot spots on the casing
Cracked or spalled refractory visible through the sight glass
Casing temperature above 80 C over a large area
snag_types.detection_method: Thermal-camera scan of the casing every month; internal inspection at the annual shutdown

severity_levels.definition: First sign of refractory wear: hot spots on the casing noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: hot spots on the casing confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: cracked or spalled refractory visible through the sight glass; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: casing temperature above 80 c over a large area; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if a casing spot exceeds 150 C or the casing paint discolours

snag_types.immediate_action: Avoid rapid load changes and schedule a refractory inspection
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if a casing spot exceeds 150 C or the casing paint discolours

pollution_effects.effect: Heat loss through the casing raises fuel burned and CO2 per unit of heat.

snag_types.name: Dye-liquor pump seal leak
symptoms: Drips of dye liquor at the pump seal
Steady leak with a puddle under the pump
Spray of hot liquor or loss of circulation pressure
root_causes: Dry running at the start of a cycle
snag_types.detection_method: Walk-round visual check and a drip count per minute; circulation pressure trend

severity_levels.definition: First sign of dye-liquor pump seal leak: drips of dye liquor at the pump seal noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: drips of dye liquor at the pump seal confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: steady leak with a puddle under the pump; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: spray of hot liquor or loss of circulation pressure; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.

Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if the leak reaches a floor drain or circulation pressure falls below the recipe minimum

snag_types.immediate_action: Contain the leak with a tray, cool and drain before touching, and book the seal replacement
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the leak reaches a floor drain or circulation pressure falls below the recipe minimum

pollution_effects.effect: Leaked dye liquor reaches the effluent stream untreated or as a shock load.
Dyes and auxiliaries are released outside the closed loop.

snag_types.name: Air filter or strainer clog
symptoms: Filter differential pressure above normal
Fan running at higher current with weaker draft
Burner starving of air with a rich flame
root_causes: Lint and dust load from the finishing area
snag_types.detection_method: Differential-pressure gauge reading against the clean value; fan current trend

severity_levels.definition: First sign of air filter or strainer clog: filter differential pressure above normal noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: filter differential pressure above normal confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: fan running at higher current with weaker draft; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: burner starving of air with a rich flame; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if the burner trips on low air or the filter housing is damaged

snag_types.immediate_action: Clean or swap the filter element at the next safe stop
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the burner trips on low air or the filter housing is damaged

pollution_effects.effect: Air starvation causes incomplete combustion and soot emissions.

snag_types.name: Stenter chain wear
symptoms: Uneven fabric width
Clicking or jerking chain with visible elongation
Clips dropping the fabric edge or the chain jumping the sprocket
root_causes: Lint and finish residue on the rails
snag_types.detection_method: Chain elongation measurement over ten links and fabric width checks at the exit

severity_levels.definition: First sign of stenter chain wear: uneven fabric width noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: uneven fabric width confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: clicking or jerking chain with visible elongation; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: clips dropping the fabric edge or the chain jumping the sprocket; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if the chain jumps the sprocket or the clips drop fabric repeatedly

snag_types.immediate_action: Reduce speed, clean and lubricate the rails, and plan the chain overhaul
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the chain jumps the sprocket or the clips drop fabric repeatedly

pollution_effects.effect: Re-processing rejected fabric adds drying energy and CO2.

snag_types.name: Heat-exchanger scaling
symptoms: Longer heating time to reach the dye-bath temperature
Approach temperature up by more than 5 C
Steam consumption per batch up 10% or more
root_causes: Hard water or poor softener regeneration
snag_types.detection_method: Heating-rate and approach-temperature trend per batch; steam per batch from the meter

severity_levels.definition: First sign of heat-exchanger scaling: longer heating time to reach the dye-bath temperature noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: longer heating time to reach the dye-bath temperature confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: approach temperature up by more than 5 c; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: steam consumption per batch up 10% or more; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if the batch cycle overruns by more than 20% or a tube leak is suspected

snag_types.immediate_action: Check the softener and the water hardness, and plan descaling
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the batch cycle overruns by more than 20% or a tube leak is suspected

pollution_effects.effect: Extra steam per batch raises boiler fuel use and CO2.
Descaling waste must be neutralised before it reaches the ETP.

snag_types.name: Padder roll misalignment
symptoms: Uneven pick-up across the width
Listing or shade variation edge to centre
Roll bearing noise and visible roll skew
snag_types.detection_method: Nip-impression test and pick-up weight checks at both edges and the centre

severity_levels.definition: First sign of padder roll misalignment: uneven pick-up across the width noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: uneven pick-up across the width confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: listing or shade variation edge to centre; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: roll bearing noise and visible roll skew; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if the shade variation causes batch rejection

snag_types.immediate_action: Adjust the nip pressure, check the roll cover, and plan re-alignment
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the shade variation causes batch rejection

pollution_effects.effect: Over-padding wastes finish chemicals that end up in the effluent.
Re-washing rejected fabric adds effluent volume.

snag_types.name: Condensate return loss
symptoms: Plume of steam from the condensate vents
Condensate return below 60% of steam raised
Boiler feed-water temperature falling with higher make-up water use
snag_types.detection_method: Feed-water temperature and make-up water meter trend; ultrasonic trap survey

severity_levels.definition: First sign of condensate return loss: plume of steam from the condensate vents noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: plume of steam from the condensate vents confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: condensate return below 60% of steam raised; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: boiler feed-water temperature falling with higher make-up water use; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if the make-up water exceeds 40% or the condensate pump has failed

snag_types.immediate_action: Isolate visibly leaking traps and book a trap survey
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the make-up water exceeds 40% or the condensate pump has failed

pollution_effects.effect: Lost condensate heat increases boiler fuel use and CO2.
More make-up water and blow-down add treated-water demand and effluent.

snag_types.name: Thermal-oil degradation
symptoms: Darker oil and a burnt smell at the expansion tank
Rising pressure drop across the heater coil
Coil hot spots or low flash point in the lab result
root_causes: Oxidation from air contact in the expansion tank
snag_types.detection_method: Annual lab analysis (viscosity, acid number, flash point) and the coil pressure-drop trend

severity_levels.definition: First sign of thermal-oil degradation: darker oil and a burnt smell at the expansion tank noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: darker oil and a burnt smell at the expansion tank confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: rising pressure drop across the heater coil; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: coil hot spots or low flash point in the lab result; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate immediately if the flash point is below the operating temperature

snag_types.immediate_action: Lower the outlet set-point and take a sample for the lab
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate immediately if the flash point is below the operating temperature

pollution_effects.effect: Coked coils reduce heat transfer and raise fuel use.
Spent thermal oil is hazardous waste and must be disposed through an authorised handler.

snag_types.name: Chemical dosing pump drift
symptoms: Recipe chemicals running out early or late
Shade or pH variation between batches
Dosing volume more than 10% off the set value
snag_types.detection_method: Timed volume test against the set point and a batch-to-batch shade check

severity_levels.definition: First sign of chemical dosing pump drift: recipe chemicals running out early or late noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: recipe chemicals running out early or late confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: shade or ph variation between batches; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: dosing volume more than 10% off the set value; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if over-dosing has released excess chemical to the drain

snag_types.immediate_action: Switch to manual dosing with a measured volume and book a calibration
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if over-dosing has released excess chemical to the drain

pollution_effects.effect: Over-dosing raises auxiliary chemicals in the effluent.

snag_types.name: Dye-liquor overflow or drain valve passing
symptoms: Liquor level falling during hold
Coloured water at the floor drain during the cycle
Visible overflow from the machine or the expansion tank
root_causes: Foaming from the wrong auxiliary dose
snag_types.detection_method: Level trend during hold and a floor-drain colour check each batch

severity_levels.definition: First sign of dye-liquor overflow or drain valve passing: liquor level falling during hold noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: liquor level falling during hold confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: coloured water at the floor drain during the cycle; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: visible overflow from the machine or the expansion tank; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if coloured liquor reaches a storm drain or outside the ETP collection

snag_types.immediate_action: Close the manual isolation valve, contain the flow, and check the level sensor
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if coloured liquor reaches a storm drain or outside the ETP collection

pollution_effects.effect: Untreated coloured liquor raises COD and colour in the discharge.
Dyes and salts are released outside the treatment path.

snag_types.name: Exhaust fan imbalance
symptoms: Rising vibration at the fan bearings
Noise and belt slip
Weak exhaust with fumes or humidity in the chamber
root_causes: Lint and finish deposits on the impeller
snag_types.detection_method: Vibration reading in mm/s on both bearings and the exhaust damper position

severity_levels.definition: First sign of exhaust fan imbalance: rising vibration at the fan bearings noticed at inspection; no measurable effect on output, energy use or emissions. Log it and watch at the next round.
Minor: rising vibration at the fan bearings confirmed; energy or quality penalty under about 2%. Plan the repair job for the next planned stop.
Moderate: noise and belt slip; fuel use, emissions or product quality measurably worse. Repair within 7 days and check every shift.
Serious: weak exhaust with fumes or humidity in the chamber; a process, safety or permit limit is at risk. Repair within 48 hours and inform the shift supervisor.
Severe or failing: trip, damage or a permit breach is imminent. Stop the machine safely, isolate, and escalate: escalate if vibration exceeds 11 mm/s or a bearing runs hot

snag_types.immediate_action: Reduce the speed if possible and book the fan service
snag_types.escalation_criteria: Escalate if vibration exceeds 11 mm/s or a bearing runs hot

pollution_effects.effect: Weak exhaust leaves fumes and VOC from finishes in the work area and raises drying energy.
